svg.text: goal: the same output whether processing in near real time or
catching up from the start; only best effort is possible (late
events, failures); wall-clock and external-service workflows are
NTP: a few ms drift after 15 minutes on a LAN, 1 ms or less
with frequent sync (David Mills); across the internet about
+/- 100 ms; NTP can fail; improving toward sub-millisecond;
cloud providers run redundant atomic and satellite clocks
Offsets order events only within a single partition; timestamps order events across streams. Fig 9-2: deposits ($10, $20) and a $25 withdrawal arrive on different
streams; round-robin processing applies the withdrawal too early, causing a false overdraft penalty. Streams must be copartitioned (or repartitioned and rekeyed) first.
Prefer producer event time when reliable; otherwise broker ingestion time.
